prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I keep palladium-catalysed C-N coupling as the first part because it is the cleanest case on the shortlist for what was new chemically and who did it. Buchwald and Hartwig turned aryl amine formation, a harsh and narrow reaction, into a general, ligand-controlled bond construction. The mechanism is settled, the method is independently confirmed in thousands of syntheses, and it runs at scale in pharmaceutical process chemistry. After round 1 I add base editing, credited to Liu alone, as a second part. Of the modality candidates it has a defined chemical reaction (deamination in an editing window), a clear originality argument (TadA evolved to act on DNA) and a credit story that can be defended with one name. Together the two parts keep the laureate list at three and pair a mature molecule-making method with a recent chemical capability, which is a better picture of the field than either alone.
statement.case_against: Round 1 gave me no evidence that C-N coupling can win alone: it was the lead of one member, and the 2010 prize for Pd-catalysed C-C coupling still invites the objection that this is a natural extension. Base editing is about a decade old, sits close to the 2020 CRISPR prize, and Liu alone leaves out Komor and Gaudelli, who did decisive experiments, and Nishida and Kondo, whose Target-AID work was contemporaneous. A Liu-only citation is a compromise on credit that I make only because of the three-name cap, and I cannot claim it is the uniquely correct attribution. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work also leaves a precedence question I have not verified.

responses.point: Linke asked why C-N coupling should be preferred over base editing and proposed a two-part prize of base editing (Liu alone) and lipid nanoparticles (Cullis, Hope).
responses.response: I take the question seriously and my move answers part of it. I do not think C-N coupling is stronger than base editing on novelty or on consequence in biology, but it is stronger on maturity and attribution. I accept Liu alone for B050, which is your own attribution, and I see this as the point where we can meet. Where I differ is the second part. Pairing two nucleic-acid-medicine topics, as you note yourself, risks Chemistry following the 2020 and 2023 prizes rather than leading with chemical principle. A pairing with a molecule-making method answers that concern and keeps the list at three people, whereas Cullis, Hope and Liu would also be three names but both parts would sit in one territory.

responses.point: Chabes prefers base editing as a defined chemical reaction, concedes it would yield to a more clearly chemical modality if the committee judged it medicine, and names Liu, Komor and Gaudelli.
responses.response: I accept your chemical case for the adenine editor, and I now judge the chemistry-versus-medicine objection to be answerable if the citation is written around the base conversion itself. My earlier unease about naming trainees stands: with a three-name cap, Liu with Komor and Gaudelli would leave no seat for C-N coupling and would still exclude Nishida and Kondo, so I prefer Liu alone. If you hold that Komor and Gaudelli must be named, then our configurations cannot be combined and I would then rather you tell me whether you could accept B050 as the single part, which I could still support over the alternatives.

responses.point: Aqvist keeps targeted protein degradation first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, keeping Handa over Ciulli, and says the weakest seat in his configuration is the third.
responses.response: Your reply on Handa versus Ciulli is persuasive on its own terms: identifying cereblon as the thalidomide target is a distinct discovery. That is exactly why I doubt one citation can cover both strands. The PROTAC concept of Crews and Deshaies was a peptide-based demonstration, and the cereblon story is a separate mechanistic discovery, so the prize would honour two lineages with three seats and still exclude Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto. I still rate B042 as my first alternative and could vote for it if it becomes the committee's clear consensus, but I do not think the credit problem is solved by your configuration.

responses.point: Brzezinski moved to B042, asks that expert reports state what is unsettled before a citation spanning PROTACs and glues is fixed, and notes the first PROTAC work used peptidic, cell-impermeable molecules.
responses.response: I agree with the request for expert input and with the point about peptidic PROTACs, which is the main reason I regard the decisive chemical step to drug-like degraders as belonging to later hands than the 2001 concept. If the expert reports separate the two strands, B042 is more likely to become a one-strand prize, and I would then reconsider it as a stand-alone part. I would also ask the expert reports on B029 to address the Kosugi precedence question so that the committee does not rely on my memory.

uncertainties: Whether the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize makes C-N coupling look redundant to a majority of the committee.
Whether Liu alone is a defensible attribution for base editing, given Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo.
Whether base editing is judged chemistry rather than medicine, and whether a decade of history is enough maturity after the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Exact precedence of Kosugi's tin-amide aminations, which I have not verified.
Whether a pairing of a mature synthetic method with a recent nucleic-acid modality can gather five votes, since no single configuration has yet shown majority support.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no known institutional or personal tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi or Liu, and I am not a close collaborator of any other credited name. My training in Masamune's group at MIT is a general stereocontrolled synthesis tradition and not a connection to any shortlisted candidate. I share a Lund affiliation with Linke and Sparr, which is not a tie to any nominee.
